lens: budget-auditor — every objection below is anchored in an arithmetic I redid myself against files on disk (byte sizes from `ls`, PNG dimensions read from the IHDR chunk, WCAG ratios computed from tokens.css, file/route counts recounted from the candidate's own newFiles list, README status strings re-read first-hand, climx MEASUREMENTS.md rows re-read first-hand). The candidate's self-reported numbers were treated as claims and checked, not carried.

feasibilityRecompute.ownSum: ROUTES (E8 ≤ 4): 3 real paths (/, /proyecto/:slug, /evidencia) + 1 mandatory router `fallback` (NotFound). Under the candidate's own conservative convention that is 4/4 — ZERO margin. Under a path-only reading it is 3/4. Either way it does not exceed. NEW FILES UNDER src/ (E8 ≤ 18): I recounted its newFiles list item by item — router.tsx, router.test.tsx, lib/assets.ts, pages/IndexPage.tsx, pages/ProjectPage.tsx, pages/ProjectPage.test.tsx, pages/EvidencePage.tsx, pages/NotFound.tsx, pages/pages.module.css, components/EvidenceChip.tsx, EvidenceChip.module.css, ClaimList.tsx, ClaimList.module.css, Figure.tsx, Figure.module.css, content.test.ts = 16. Its scopeBudget number is correct. I checked for unlisted files it needs and found none that land under src/: public/404.html and public/img/*.png are outside src/ (public/ does not exist today — verified, it is created new, correctly outside the E8 unit), and main.tsx / app.tsx / reset.css / content.ts / ProjectCard.tsx / ProjectCard.module.css / ProjectCard.test.tsx / app.module.css are all MODIFICATIONS of files already on disk (all eight verified present). Margin = 2 files, but the design's own pattern pairs every component with a .module.css (EvidenceChip, ClaimList, Figure all pair), so 2 files = exactly ONE more component before K7 fires. M3(a): baseline verified in the objective at 62.40 kB gzip JS; climx — which ships this same router plus five pages, a fetch/cache layer, an ARIA combobox and a geo layer — measures 66.66 KB gzip (MEASUREMENTS.md line 30, read first-hand). A ~120-line router + 4 pages + 4 small components on a 62.40 kB React baseline lands in the 64-70 kB bracket. Against 150 KB that is ~45% of bound. M3(b), MY arithmetic, not its: real byte sizes from disk — trazado_1.png 167,722 B (IHDR: 1275x721), phyriadfg_multigpu.png 89,350 B (1949x662), phyriadfg_pipeline.png 64,286 B (2063x507). Shell per view = JS ~69,632 B + CSS ~2,560 B + HTML ~1,024 B ≈ 73,216 B. Heaviest view = /proyecto/phyriager: 167,722 + 73,216 = 240,938 B = 235 KB against a 500 KB bound → 47% of budget, 265 KB headroom. Second: /proyecto/phyriadfg with BOTH diagrams (M-C copies both) = 153,636 + 73,216 = 226,852 B = 222 KB. Index and /evidencia carry no images: ~72 KB each. PNGs do not gzip, so these are transferred bytes as required. E3: nothing here needs a package absent from package.json — the router is hand-rolled with zero deps, node:fs is a builtin available to Vitest, sharp is explicitly refused. Verified against the dependencies block (react + react-dom only) and the devDependencies block (vitest, jsdom, @testing-library/*, jsx-a11y all present).
underpricedItems: M3(b) second-heaviest view: the candidate prices /proyecto/phyriadfg at ~162 KB counting only multigpu.png (89,350 B), but its own M-C milestone copies phyriadfg_pipeline.png (64,286 B) into public/img/ as well. If the phyriadfg dossier renders both diagrams the real figure is ~222 KB, a 37% under-price. It does not threaten the 500 KB bound — it is a 60 KB error inside a 265 KB headroom — but it is the exact class of miss the auditor is here for, and it is in the one metric the candidate claims to have priced most carefully.

M4 test-count and existing-suite breakage: the candidate reports 'Test count goes 6 → ~21 (6 existing + 9 router + ~6 new)', assuming all six current tests survive. I opened the existing suite: src/components/ProjectCard.test.tsx contains 2 of those 6 tests, and it constructs a `const base: Project` literal with `{name, tag, description, sourceUrl}` and asserts a link named 'Source: GitHub'. Milestone M-B rewrites src/content.ts's `Project` type and rebuilds ProjectCard as the evidence row — that file will fail BOTH `tsc --noEmit` (the type literal no longer conforms) and the two assertions. M4 is an unconditional gate (K3), so this is unpriced work on the critical path. Bounded: it is a modification of an existing file, so it costs nothing against E8. Also, the router suite is 10 `it(` blocks in climx, not 9.

E8 route margin: 'closesUnderE8: true' is reported without noting that under the candidate's own (correct, conservative) convention of counting the mandatory fallback, the route budget is consumed exactly — 4/4, zero margin. Adding any route at all is a K7 disqualification, and the design's own weakestPoint concedes /evidencia is the route it would cut first.
E8 file granularity: 16/18 is reported as a 2-file margin, but the design pairs every component with a .module.css. The effective margin is one component, not two files.

scorecard.justification: Coverage is enforced by the compiler, not by care: `Claim.evidence` is a required field of a discriminated union under TS strict (E5 confirms strict), so an unbacked assertion fails `tsc --noEmit`, and `EvidenceChip` being the only printer of backing makes 'rendered assertion' and 'evidence affordance' the same JSX node — which is what makes M1's frozen enumeration unit actually countable rather than judged. Two enumerating instruments (content.test.ts walking every claim + fs-checking every figure.file; ProjectPage.test.tsx rendering all 5 dossiers). Name and status modelled as claims covers the full unit. Conditional on repo publicity (3 of 5 repos unverifiable from disk), but I note the fraction is degenerate under pressure: the declared fallback of deleting unbacked claims preserves 100% by definition while shrinking what the page says. That is the frozen metric's shape, not this candidate's fault, and the candidate declares it.

5/5, and I verified all five literal strings myself against the sources rather than against the candidate: Phyriager README line 16 'Status: `0.1.0-experimental`'; PhyriadFG README '`0.4.0-experimental` · Windows · student-built'; Phynned README '`0.2.0-experimental`'; PHarvard README State table '**runs on silicon.** Full instruction set verified on the board, 2026-08-01'; climx live per the objective. All five match. Rendering the literal string converts M2's instrument from an interpretive diff into an exact-string diff, which is the strongest possible form of the frozen instrument. The design structurally cannot render five equal polished tiles — the rows carry five different evidence kinds — so the M2=0 failure mode is closed by construction.

Both thresholds cleared by my own arithmetic with roughly half the budget unspent: (a) 64-70 kB gzip JS against 150 KB (~45%), bracketed by two measured neighbours (62.40 kB baseline, 66.66 kB for a strictly heavier climx); (b) heaviest view 235 KB against 500 KB (47%), from real on-disk PNG bytes. The index — the entry view the 20-second workload actually hits — carries no images at ~72 KB, the lightest view on the site. The design also declines the one thing that would have blown this bound: it copies three PNGs, not the six audit_frame files (which sum to 398,302 B and would put a single view at ~460 KB). Score is for fitness to the threshold; the 37% under-price on the phyriadfg view is logged as a defect, not a deduction, because it does not approach the bound.

No structural blocker found and one real corroboration: I diffed portfolio/eslint.config.js against climx/eslint.config.js and they are byte-identical (same tseslint.config shape, same react-hooks + jsx-a11y recommended rules), so the candidate's claim that the ported router's useEffect passes under 'the identical flat config' is TRUE first-hand and that risk is genuinely low. Deducted one for the unnamed break: src/components/ProjectCard.test.tsx (2 of the 6 existing tests) fails typecheck and assertions once content.ts's `Project` type is rewritten in M-B, and the candidate's M4 estimate counts all 6 existing tests as surviving. The Figure/jsx-a11y anchor risk is named honestly and is real (an anchor wrapping only an img has no accessible name under the recommended set).

(c) I recomputed all four sRGB contrast ratios from tokens.css myself: #111111 on #ffffff = 18.88:1; #5b5b5b on #ffffff = 6.79:1; #5b5b5b on #fafafa = 6.51:1; #2255cc on #ffffff = 6.48:1 — the candidate's 18.7 / 6.8 / 6.5 / 6.5 are correct to rounding, and its claim of adding no new colour token means these are final. (b) I verified the deficit it claims to fix: app.tsx today renders the footer as `Text as="span"` (line 40) and has no `<nav>`; Header.tsx does render `<header>` and app.tsx does render `<Stack as="main">`. So the design provably supplies the two missing landmarks, and reset.css today has no .skip-link rules while climx's does. Deducted one for (a): the Figure anchor risk is live and unresolved, and M5 requires all three parts.

My own deletion recount against GitHub Pages at /portfolio/, opening each donor file: (1) router.tsx — read in full, BASE derives from import.meta.env.BASE_URL which portfolio's vite.config already sets to '/portfolio/'; delete it and 2 of 3 routes cease to exist. Structural. (2) 404.html + the main.tsx lines 7-18 restore block — I confirmed portfolio/src/main.tsx has NO such block and public/ does not exist; the objective itself (M6/AT0 fix 3) names the 404 deep-link shim as structural under this referent. Counting the pair as ONE resource matches the objective's own §Verified list, which catalogues the shim as a single entry. Structural. (3) the BASE_URL asset helper lifted from EstadoCard's estadoImg — the objective explicitly blesses this mechanism; delete it and every figure resolves to /img/... instead of /portfolio/img/... Structural, though the reused code is a 3-line function. Under the metric AS WRITTEN ('resources doing structural work in the portfolio', no requirement that this candidate ported them), tokens.css, the primitives and reset.css also count, putting the honest total at ≥5 against a target of ≥4. Deducted one because the candidate's claimed 4 rests on an internally inconsistent rule (see F2): it excludes primitives and tokens.css as 'already present' while counting reset.css, which is equally already present on disk. Applied consistently, its own contribution is 3 — the K2 floor exactly, one below the M6 target. M6 is a declared floor, not a maximand, so nothing is gained above 4 anyway.

attackOnCentralClaim:
SURVIVES, with one falsified sub-claim and one materially understated limitation.

The claim — that making evidence a required TYPED field, so an unbacked assertion does not compile, buys more credibility than polish — is not rhetoric here, and I checked the mechanism rather than the assertion. TS strict is confirmed by E5; a required field on a discriminated union does hard-fail `tsc --noEmit`; `npm run typecheck` is already in package.json and is an M4 gate command, so the enforcement runs on the same gate the objective scores. The claim is real, and it is aimed at P1, the top of the frozen priority order.

The competitor is NOT a strawman. It attacks 'five equal polished tiles', and the frozen objective itself says in M2 that exactly that page 'scores 0 here'. Attacking the failure mode the objective names is fair play, not shadowboxing.

WHERE IT WINS: the reader who clicks through. A screening engineer who opens /proyecto/pharvard meets 'runs on silicon. Full instruction set verified on the board, 2026-08-01' — a string I confirmed verbatim in that README's State table — beside 1,409 LUT4 (21%) and a link into the repo. Two of the five projects have independently checkable evidence I verified first-hand (PHarvard's README states its own URL and records the 2026-08-01 rename with redirects intact; climx is live and its MEASUREMENTS.md carries dated instrumented rows). Against P1 that reader is exactly the one who matters.

WHERE IT EMBARRASSES ITSELF — TWO READERS, and the candidate only names one:
(1) The 20-second reader. The design's own weakestPoint concedes the page can read as 'weather website and a toy processor' in the workload's stated window, because ordering by provability puts the two profile-matching projects third and fourth and the operator's most impressive number last. This is a knowing, declared trade against P1, and it is defensible on the frozen priority — but it costs the exact thing the named use case cares about.
(2) The reader it does NOT name, and this is the sharper hit. Its central structural bet is that /proyecto/:slug is 'the URL a CV link or an application should point at'. climx's own MEASUREMENTS.md — the same file the candidate quotes for its FATAL percent-escape row — records, first-hand and undisputed: 'deep links devuelven HTTP 404 + HTML del shim a clientes sin JS (crawlers, unfurlers de enlaces). Es inherente a una SPA estática en Pages sin prerender'. So the dossier URL previews as nothing in a mail client, Slack, or LinkedIn unfurl, and reads as an HTTP 404 to a crawler — for precisely the three arrival paths the frozen workload names ('a GitHub profile, a CV link, or an application'). The candidate read that document, cited a different row from it, and did not surface this one. The claim survives; its most load-bearing affordance is weaker than presented.

Third, smaller: one of the five climx numbers it commits to printing is falsified by the source it cites (see F3 on ~350 B). A design whose thesis is 'an unbacked claim does not compile' shipping a superseded figure is the most expensive kind of small error it could make.

I verified every rendered asset by byte size and IHDR header: phyriadfg_multigpu.png 89,350 B (1949x662), phyriadfg_pipeline.png 64,286 B (2063x507), trazado_1.png 167,722 B (1275x721). The candidate's claim that it opened pipeline.png first-hand and found it 2063x507 is CORROBORATED by my own header read — that is a claim the frozen objective explicitly could not verify, and it checks out. It also refuses four things it is not entitled to: the missing PHarvard board photo, a climx screenshot, the stale Lighthouse numbers, and climx's contradictory test count. Refusing flattering unavailable content is the opposite of K1.

Zero under the strictest reading, comfortable under the metric as written. Applying the candidate's OWN already-present exclusion rule consistently strips reset.css and leaves router + shim + asset-helper = 3, exactly at the floor. Under M6's literal wording the count is ≥5. It does not breach K2 on any reading, but it has no room under the strict one.

killCriteria.criterion: K3 — cannot pass the M4 gate
killCriteria.margin: Thin. No structural blocker: eslint config is byte-identical to a donor that passes with the same router, typecheck/lint/test/build all already exist as scripts, zero new deps. But two of the six existing tests plus one existing type literal (src/components/ProjectCard.test.tsx, `const base: Project`) break the moment M-B rewrites content.ts's Project type, and the candidate's M4 estimate assumes all six survive. killCriteria.criterion: K4 — renders a claim its own README/docs do not support
killCriteria.margin: NEGATIVE on one line item. The candidate commits to printing '~350 B gzip per municipio file' as a climx number. I opened MEASUREMENTS.md: the relevant row is a before/after pair reading 'forecast 3/1 = 344 B gz | 463 B gz (<< 200 KB, M4)' — 344 B is the SUPERSEDED value and the current measured payload is 463 B gz. Printing ~350 B is a statement about a project that its own current source does not support, which is a K4 hit and also trips the objective's quality veto ('no statement about a project contradicts that project's own source'). Bounded to one string and repairable by using 463 B, but as written it does not clear. Its other four climx figures I verified and they hold: 9,852 records → 2,463 files (line 14), 66.66 KB gzip bundle (line 30).

killCriteria.criterion: K5 — not measurable with E5's toolchain
killCriteria.margin: Adequate. Every metric has an instrument that exists on this machine: M1 and M4 via the four npm scripts already in package.json; M2 by string diff against five READMEs I re-read; M3(a) via `npm run build`, M3(b) via `npm run preview` + network panel, both the objective's named instruments; M5(c) by arithmetic on tokens.css, which I reproduced to four values. Nothing depends on Lighthouse, correctly. The declared limitation is real and honestly stated: two of the four M6 sub-items (the shim, and the asset helper's base prefix) are host behaviours only observable on a real Pages deploy, and Vite preview's SPA fallback masks the shim. That rests on the objective's own AT0 fix 3 referent rather than a local measurement — and since E6 records no remote and no commits, that referent is counterfactual for every candidate equally, not a defect of this one.

killCriteria.criterion: K6 — requires a new runtime dependency, service, key, or recurring cost
killCriteria.margin: Large. Dependencies block stays react + react-dom (verified). The router is hand-rolled with zero deps. content.test.ts's fs check uses node:fs, a builtin that resolves under Vitest even with environment:'jsdom' (Vitest runs in Node). @testing-library/react and jsdom are already in devDependencies. It explicitly refuses `sharp` for WebP conversion on E3 grounds and eats the PNG bytes instead — the correct call, since the byte budget absorbs them at 47%.

killCriteria.criterion: K7 — exceeds E8 (> 4 routes or > 18 new files under src/)
killCriteria.margin: Files: 16/18 by my own recount of its list, but only ONE component-pair of headroom given its .tsx+.module.css pattern. Routes: 3 real paths + 1 mandatory fallback = 4/4 under its own conservative convention, i.e. zero margin. It does not exceed either bound, and its scopeBudget numbers are honest — but this, not payload, is where the design sits closest to a wall.

smugglingCheck:
CLEAN — checked item by item against the FORBIDDEN and DROPPED lists, including the state photographs specifically.

FORBIDDEN (public/img/estados/*.webp): nothing in the candidate references estados/, .webp, or any Mexican-geography photo. The one place a smuggle could hide is the EstadoCard port, and I opened climx/src/components/EstadoCard.tsx to check what actually crosses. What crosses is `estadoImg(ides)` → generalized to `asset(path)`, and the `onError` degrade — and the frozen objective names EXACTLY these ('the object-fit: cover card CSS, lazy loading, the onError degrade, the BASE_URL asset helper') as explicitly NOT forbidden and encouraged when pointed at the operator's own images. The candidate points them at operator-produced TikZ diagrams and an annotated agent frame. Non-smuggle by the objective's own words.

Stronger evidence of discipline, not weaker: the port DROPS `.img` and `overflow: hidden` from EstadoCard.module.css because the index carries no images, and it REVERSES climx's two image decisions rather than inheriting them — alt goes from `alt=\"\"` (correct for a decorative state photo) to a real Spanish description (correct for a figure that carries the evidence), and loading goes from 'lazy' to 'eager'. Both reversals are only justifiable if the image's role changed from decoration to proof, which is the opposite of smuggling the photographs' role.

DROPPED drivers: no fetchWithCache, no useFetch, no staleness hooks, no geo layer, no SearchCombobox, no AgeBanner/ForecastCard/skyIcon/NearestMunicipio/CommonsGallery — I checked the climxPorts list for all of them and none appears. The MEASUREMENTS.md and README.md entries are explicitly typed as CONTENT (prose and numbers about climx as a project), not as the data layer, and the candidate itself refuses to count them toward M6 for that reason.

One borderline I examined and cleared: the ported router carries a `useEffect` + listener Set, which is the only stateful runtime machinery crossing over. That is the router — the objective calls it 'its strongest reusable asset' — not a speculative data layer with no consumer.
optimalityHonesty:
No unscoped optimality claim found. I read the candidate specifically for absolute 'optimal'/'best'/'novel' assertions and every superlative it makes is scoped to a named set: 'the strongest presentation numbers in the whole pool' (the pool), 'the single most impressive-sounding number the operator owns' (the operator's own set), 'the highest-value missing asset for this design specifically' (explicitly self-scoped), 'its strongest reusable asset' (quoting the objective's own wording back), 'the WEAKEST of my four' (self-scoped, and self-incriminating). It never claims to be the best candidate, never claims the evidence-index angle is optimal, and never claims novelty.

The central thesis is stated as a BET with its cost priced ('This design bets that... and it accepts the cost that the resulting order puts the operator's most impressive-sounding result last'), which is the honest form. Its self-scores are argued from measured neighbours rather than asserted, and where it cannot measure — the two host-dependent M6 items — it says so unprompted: 'I claim it on the objective's declared referent, not on a local measurement.' It also volunteers the counter-argument against its own weakest M6 entry and states what its score falls to if struck.

The nearest thing to an overclaim is not an optimality claim at all but the M6 accounting inconsistency logged as F2 below, and the falsified ~350 B figure logged as F3. F5: none.

defects.finding: K4 / quality-veto hit on a printed number. The candidate commits to rendering '~350 B gzip per municipio file' among the five climx figures it will print. I opened climx/docs/planning/MEASUREMENTS.md: the row is a before/after pair, 'forecast 3/1 = 344 B gz' → '463 B gz (<< 200 KB, M4)'. 344 B is the superseded value; the current measured per-municipio forecast payload is 463 B gz. As written, the page would state a figure the project's own current source contradicts — the exact condition the objective's quality veto fails a page for, regardless of every metric. Repairable by one string, but this design's whole thesis is that unbacked claims cannot ship, and it caught climx's README-vs-MEASUREMENTS test-count contradiction while missing this one in the same file.

The central claim's most load-bearing affordance is materially understated. The design designates /proyecto/:slug as 'the URL a CV link or an application should point at' and counts the 404 shim as structural on that basis. climx's MEASUREMENTS.md — which the candidate demonstrably read and cites for the percent-escape FATAL — records under 'Declarados y NO corregidos': 'INFO — deep links devuelven HTTP 404 + HTML del shim a clientes sin JS (crawlers, unfurlers de enlaces). Es inherente a una SPA estática en Pages sin prerender.' So the dossier URL renders no preview in a mail client, Slack or LinkedIn unfurl and returns HTTP 404 to a crawler — for exactly the arrival paths the frozen workload names ('a GitHub profile, a CV link, or an application'). The shim remains structural under the objective's declared referent (that stands), but the design's presentation of the deep link as the shareable artifact is stronger than the donor's own measured record supports, and the candidate did not surface a limitation it had in hand.

M6 accounting is internally inconsistent in the direction that helps it. The candidate excludes climx's primitives and tokens.css from its M6 count on the explicit ground that they are 'ALREADY PRESENT, not ported by this design' — a rule I accept. It then counts reset.css, which is equally already present: F:\Phyriad\projects\portfolio\src\styles\reset.css exists on disk today with the header comment 'Minimal modern reset (shared pattern with climx)'. The design re-adds five blocks to a file it already has; that is a modification of an existing climx-derived resource, not a new structural port. Applying its own rule consistently gives M6 = 3 — the K2 floor exactly, and one BELOW the M6 ≥ 4 target it claims to meet. (Under M6's literal wording, which requires no authorship by the candidate, the true count is ≥5 and the target is met comfortably; the defect is the inconsistent middle position, which the candidate half-anticipates by calling reset.css its weakest entry without noticing this is the actual reason it is weak.)

M3(b) second-heaviest view under-priced by 37%. Candidate: '/proyecto/phyriadfg ≈ 162 KB (multigpu.png 89,350 B)'. Its own M-C milestone copies BOTH phyriadfg_multigpu.png (89,350 B) and phyriadfg_pipeline.png (64,286 B) into public/img/, and its evidence model names 'the PhyriadFG TikZ diagrams' plural. Both on one view = 153,636 B images + ~73,216 B shell = 226,852 B ≈ 222 KB. Immaterial to the verdict — the 500 KB bound is cleared at 47% by the true heaviest view (/proyecto/phyriager, 240,938 B ≈ 235 KB by my arithmetic, which matches its ~240 KB) — but it is a miscount in the line item it claims to have priced most carefully.

M4 test arithmetic wrong in two places, one of them on the critical path. (a) The candidate says the climx router suite is '9 tests'; grep -c 'it(' on climx/src/router/router.test.tsx returns 10. (b) More materially, '6 → ~21 (6 existing + 9 router + ~6 new)' assumes all six current tests survive. Two of the six live in src/components/ProjectCard.test.tsx, which declares 'const base: Project = { name, tag, description, sourceUrl }' and asserts a link named 'Source: GitHub'. Milestone M-B rewrites content.ts's Project type and rebuilds ProjectCard as the evidence row — that file then fails BOTH typecheck and its assertions. M4 is an unconditional gate (K3). Cost is an in-place edit of an existing file, so zero E8 impact, but it is unpriced work the design does not name among its 'two named risks rather than a blanket claim'.

Scope margin reported without its real granularity, and one E7 tension. 'closesUnderE8: true' with 16/18 files and 4/4 routes is arithmetically correct (I recounted both), but the route budget is consumed exactly — zero headroom — and the file margin is one component, not two files, because every component in the design ships as a .tsx + .module.css pair. Separately and interpretively: Figure.tsx is specified with 'explicit width/height' on the img, and E7 forbids hardcoded px outside src/styles/tokens.css. Whether an HTML intrinsic-size attribute counts as a hardcoded px is genuinely ambiguous and I do not assert a violation, only the tension.

salvageables: Evidence as a REQUIRED field of a typed discriminated union, so an unbacked project assertion fails `tsc --noEmit`. This moves M1 from a discipline the author must sustain to a condition the existing M4 gate already enforces — no new tooling, no new dependency.

`EvidenceChip` as the ONLY component permitted to print a claim's backing, which makes 'rendered assertion' and 'evidence affordance' the same JSX node by construction. This is what makes M1's frozen enumeration unit mechanically countable instead of a judgement call.

Rendering each project's status as the LITERAL string copied from its README, which converts M2's named instrument from an interpretive diff into an exact-string diff. I verified all five strings against their READMEs and they hold — the technique is sound and it closes M2's stated failure mode (five equal polished tiles) structurally.

content.test.ts asserting that every `figure.file` actually exists on disk under public/, via Node fs inside Vitest. A broken image becomes a red test rather than a live-site defect, at the cost of one builtin import and no new dependency.

The `provisional` evidence kind: rendering a project's own published self-disclaimer AS the evidence, rather than dropping the project or softening the wording. Verified as grounded — Phynned's README line 232 states the dataset is 'provisional and under re-validation'. It is a way to carry a weak project honestly instead of silently.

The anti-padding accounting rules it imposes on itself: counting 404.html + the main.tsx restore block as ONE M6 resource because the inventory catalogues them as one; refusing to count router.test.tsx, NotFound.tsx and the app shell because their deletion tests are either the router's wearing a second name or scored against the repository rather than the page. Whatever the M6 target, that rule set is the right shape for scoring reuse.

Refusing to print the flattering-but-stale numbers by name: the Lighthouse 90/100 and 100/98 figures (measured against the pre-rename project-tw URL) and climx's test count (README says 41, MEASUREMENTS says 51/51 — I confirmed both, the contradiction is real). Naming the specific reason each is withheld is more useful than the numbers would have been.

The M-A milestone shape: land the router, the shim and the 404 restore with a single '/' route rendering today's page untouched, so the router's isolated gzip cost is measurable against the 62.40 kB baseline BEFORE any content changes. That sequencing turns M3(a) into a controlled measurement instead of a post-hoc total.
Generalizing `estadoImg(ides)` into `asset(path)` — decoupling the BASE_URL prefix mechanism from the forbidden state photographs, which is precisely the split the frozen objective asks for.

Deliberately reversing climx's two image decisions with a stated reason: real Spanish alt text (the figure carries the information here, so `alt=""` would be a lie) and eager loading with explicit dimensions for an above-the-fold proof figure. Inheriting a donor's choices unexamined is the usual failure of a port.

(2) Default branch names for every repo, on which the `doc` evidence kind's deep links depend — the candidate declares it did not verify these either. (3) The actual gzip output of any build: I did not run `npm run build`, `npm run preview`, `npm test`, `npm run lint` or `npm run typecheck` (no file may be written and dist/ is a write). attackOnCentralClaim:
The claim is that a REQUIRED, typed `evidence` field means an unbacked claim 'does not compile', buying more credibility than polish. It survives PARTIALLY, and the part that fails is the load-bearing half.

What survives: making `evidence` non-optional genuinely makes OMISSION impossible, and that is a durable property no amount of care gives you. I verified climx's Router types (`fallback: ComponentType`, non-optional; `Route = {path, page}`), so the TS-strict enforcement argument is mechanically sound in kind. Modelling name and status as claims too is the right move against M1's enumeration unit, and it works. M2 is unassailable: I diffed all five READMEs and the literal strings match, including Phynned's own 'must not be cited as validated' banner (README lines 232-237, verified verbatim) rendered as a first-class `provisional` evidence kind rather than quietly dropped.

What does not survive: the type system enforces PRESENCE, not VERIFIABILITY. `{kind:'doc', url:'https://github.com/Swately/Phynned/blob/main/docs/reports/EMPIRICAL_EVIDENCE_SUMMARY.md'}` pointing at a 404 compiles, passes both described test files (content.test.ts checks https and on-disk figure existence only), and renders on the page as proof. M1 asks for 'one click from VERIFIABLE evidence'; a non-optional field delivers 'one click from a string'. The only thing that actually enforces M1 is the M-D manual fetch sweep — discipline wearing a toolchain's clothes. Compounding it: 4 of the 5 evidence kinds are self-citation. `number` links to the project's own doc restating the number, `doc` links to the project's own file, `figure` renders an image the project made, `provisional` is an admission. Only `live` is independent, and only climx has it. So a route advertised as 'Todas las afirmaciones del sitio' is, for four fifths of the page, a bibliography of self-references — an internally consistent ledger, not an audit.

The implicit competitor — five equal polished tiles — is real, not a strawman: the objective itself names it ('a page that renders five projects as five equal polished tiles scores 0 here'). Against THAT competitor this design wins outright.

The competitor it never names, and should have: a well-written GitHub profile README. It is in English (O1's audience), it lives where the reader already is, every repo link is self-verifying by construction, README status lines ARE the source of truth so M2 is 5/5 free, and it costs zero routes, zero files, and no deploy. For the named 20-second workload it plausibly beats this page. The one thing it cannot do — and this design can — is stop claim drift: there is no test suite on a profile README that fails when an assertion loses its backing. That is this design's honest, narrow, real win.

Where it wins: a skeptical senior engineer who clicks through, has seen ten inflated portfolios, and rewards a page that grades its own evidence and prints 'do not cite this number' on its most impressive result. Where it embarrasses itself: the 20-second cold read the objective names as its workload. A recruiter lands on a SPANISH index whose top row is a municipal weather site and whose second is a 2.08 MHz FPGA CPU, while the two projects matching the profile line they just read ('infraestructura de alto rendimiento y de agentes LLM') sit third and fourth. The candidate states this cost itself, precisely, in weakestPoint — I confirm it rather than discover it.

Consumability: the honest competitor is never named. salvageables: Making `evidence` a REQUIRED field of a typed `Claim` so an assertion with no backing fails `tsc --noEmit` — omission-proofing by the toolchain rather than by discipline. The guarantee is narrower than claimed (presence, not validity), but omission-proofing is real and durable.
